Roku Stock Is Sliding to 2018 Lows. Analysts Disagree on Its Future By Dec. 19, 2018 1:10 p.m. ET Order Reprints Roku TV Courtesy of Roku Text size
As Roku ’s (ROKU) shares have pulled back— way back—to close out 2018, more questions about exactly what kind of opportunity the stock provides have emerged.
Among the latest: Tuesday’s report from SunTrust Robinson Humphrey, which initiated coverage of the streaming TV company with a Hold rating and a $36 price target that isn’t too far about current levels. The shares were recently up 2.2% to around $32, well below Factset’s average target just above $60 and in the area of 52-week lows $3 lower.
Analyst Matthew Thornton likes Roku for reasons including its position as a pure streaming TV business, its international opportunity, and the possibility that it might be able to find more licensing partners to build TVs that contain its software—or even a possible buyer . Newsletter Sign-up
But it expects competition, notably from Amazon.com (AMZN) and Apple (AAPL), as well as cable operators, to stiffen. And it thinks the market’s expectation of revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization could be too optimistic.
Shares of Roku, dowh 38% in 2018, now sit at less than half of fall highs of around $72. The company’s fourth-quarter outlook, reported in early November, helped the slide along . Recommended Reading
